item.title: Activity & Interpretation Plan Consultant
Structural Engineer
item.description:
Advertised value: GBP 15,000 Status: active Deadline: 2026-11-30T12:00:00Z
Thetford Town Council wishes to appoint a Structural Engineer with demonstrable experience in historic buildings, conservation projects and traditional construction.
The successful consultant will assess the structural condition of the building, develop repair recommendations, contribute to design development and support the wider consultant team in delivering a viable and fundable project.
The Structural Engineer will provide technical support throughout the Development Phase and assist in the preparation of documentation required for planning, listed building consent, cost planning and future funding submissions.

item.title: Love Your Town Cleethorpes 2027
item.description:
Advertised value: GBP 24,000 Status: active Deadline: 2026-11-30T10:00:00Z
North East Lincolnshire Council (NELC) is seeking applications from suitably experienced, and qualified event organisers to co-ordinate, plan, manage and deliver a daytime event for Cleethorpes town centre with the theme being 'Love Your Town'. The date for this event is to be held during February 2027. Please note that separate events will also be held for Immingham and Grimsby and therefore some liaison regarding dates for all three events will be required to avoid any clashes. NELC is seeking to appoint an independent event organiser to deliver 'Love Cleethorpes' on our behalf in February 2027. This town centre event should feature family fun activities, live music, and entertainment etc. Specifically, the aims of the provider are to: • Encourage footfall into Cleethorpes town centre during a time when typically, footfall is low and the slowest period for retail as consumers recover from Christmas spending. • Be a great family day out with free activities to participate in. • Deliver content which showcases local talent as well as regional and potentially national performers. • Showcase local retailers and traders including food and hospitality businesses. • Deliver a market selling food, drinks, crafts, and products from primarily local providers. • Bring collaboration between retailers, hospitality businesses, educational establishments, and community groups.

item.title: CA18634 - RFQ 2026/46 - NMANDD PEACEPLUS "Thriving Together" - Celebrating Cultures and Diversity - 3.2 Creative Language Exchange
item.description:
Advertised value: GBP 10,154 Status: active Deadline: 2026-12-01T12:00:00Z
Competent and creative suppliers are hereby invited to tender for the design, development, and delivery of an engaging Creative language exchange programme. The project will deliver an inclusive Creative Language Exchange programme that uses music and cultural sharing to bring people together. Participants will learn songs in different languages, explore diverse cultures, and share their own experiences in a welcoming environment. Working towards a public performance, the programme will celebrate linguistic and cultural diversity while promoting inclusion, intercultural understanding, and belonging. The programme aims to strengthen community connections, support the integration of minority communities, and build more inclusive and cohesive communities across the district.
To access this competition:
Registered: Login to https://suppliers.multiquote.com and view the opportunity CA18634.
Not registered: Visit https://suppliers.multiquote.com then register and quote CA18634 as the reason for registration.
Any queries please contact MultiQuote on 020 3920 8054.

item.title: GB-Middlesbrough: Borderlands Phase 2 Evaluation
item.description:
Advertised value: GBP 25,000 Status: active Deadline: 2026-11-16T17:00:00Z
Borderlands is seeking to appoint an experienced independent evaluator or team of evaluators to support the evaluation of its programme in the period 2026 - 2029.
We are looking for an evaluator or team of evaluators who can work collaboratively with our team, consortium partners and Community Steering Group to understand the impact of our work, strengthen our approach to monitoring and evaluation, and generate meaningful learning that informs programme development.
The evaluation should combine robust quantitative data with rich qualitative evidence, helping us understand not only what we deliver and who we reach, but also the difference our work makes to individuals, communities, artists and the wider creative ecology.
Additional information: The contracting authority considers that this contract may be suitable for economic operators that are small or medium enterprises (SMEs). However, any selection of tenderers will be based solely on the criteria set out for the procurement.

item.title: Swanley Park Footpath Refurbishment
item.description:
Advertised value: GBP 20,000 Status: active Deadline: 2026-11-30T12:00:00Z
Swanley Town Council is seeking suitably qualified and experienced contractors to undertake the excavation, removal, reconstruction and improvement of two existing footpaths. The project aims to improve accessibility, durability and the overall quality of the footpath network through the installation of wider, fit-for-purpose pathways that meet the requirements of their intended use.
The works will comprise the following:
Footpath One
Footpath One extends approximately 355.4 linear metres and will broadly follow the alignment of the existing footpath. The pathway will be widened to provide a finished width of approximately 2.5 metres, excluding edging. The construction must be suitable for occasional vehicular access, with the appropriate sub-base and construction specification provided to accommodate this requirement.
Footpath Two
Footpath Two currently measures approximately 29 linear metres and will be extended to approximately 62.3 linear metres. The completed pathway will provide a finished width of approximately 2 metres, excluding edging, improving the provision and usability of the route.
Surfacing Options and Construction Requirements
The Council is currently exploring a range of surfacing options for the proposed footpaths, including self-binding gravel, tarmac and block paving. Contractors may be required to consider the suitability, durability, maintenance requirements, accessibility and whole-life costs associated with these options to help inform the Council's final decision on the preferred surfacing materials.
The appointed contractor will be expected to undertake the necessary excavation and removal of existing footpath materials, prepare the underlying formation, install an appropriate sub-base and construct the new footpaths in accordance with the agreed specification. The works will also include suitable edging, finishing details and any associated reinstatement required to leave the completed pathways in a safe, stable and serviceable condition.
All works must be carried out to an appropriate professional standard, with due consideration given to site conditions, public safety, drainage, accessibility and the long-term performance of the finished surfaces. The contractor will be responsible for ensuring that the construction methods and materials used are suitable for the intended use of each footpath.
The Council is seeking a cost-effective and durable solution that provides improved pedestrian routes, meets the operational requirements of the site and offers good long-term value for money.
Arrange for a site visit if required by contacting (George) gbrooker@swanleytowncouncil.gov.uk
Apply by sending your quote to (Ryan) rhayman@swanleytowncouncil.gov.uk
